boundaries.credentialOwner: DSH credentials and pi-ai OAuth; never request, log or export grants
boundaries.transportOwner: DSH llm-pi-ai; no second general Copilot adapter
boundaries.diagnostics: Repository checks only; no live profile, credential, network or model calls
boundaries.attribution: Assisted-by identifies the actual assisting tool; never infer a co-author from a model provider

authorization.purpose: OAuth lifecycle, grant normalization, route projection and account availability
authorization.risk: status and describeGitHubCopilotProviderProfile are read-only; reconcile is an explicit stored-snapshot settings write, not OAuth refresh or capability proof. Configured credentials do not prove transport readiness.

models.purpose: Catalog lag, GPT-6 temporary route and ownership restoration
models.risk: Raw preimage/postimage and revision/epoch guards protect owned writes. Legacy or changed ownership conflicts preserve state for review; never force adoption or discard a journal automatically.

search.purpose: Inline native search and the optional ctx.web provider
search.risk: Registration does not select the global Web provider. Preserve file delegation, protocol/account gates and no implicit fallback.

client.purpose: Models provider card, device-code copy UX and strict Remote results
client.risk: Use synthetic device codes. Element-tree tests are not browser interaction or activation evidence.

compatibility.purpose: Supported DSH seams, tool schemas and exact upstream fixture checks
compatibility.risk: A package version alone cannot prove a controlled Core patch; test every declared exact upstream commit.

tooling.purpose: Agent contract, preflight, verification, packaging and attribution
tooling.risk: Machine reports must distinguish not checked from failed and never claim live runtime or release success.

release.purpose: Version alignment and immutable GitHub prerelease/release delivery
release.risk: Requires explicit release approval, green CI, a fresh annotated tag and verified remote checksums; never reuse tags.
